subject: Production: Elevated 5xx/429 rate — backpressure & retry storm analysis
messages:
From: Jared Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <infra@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood — urgent

Hi Soojin,

We are seeing a significant spike in 5xx and 429 responses to our production traffic starting ~07:55 PT. Throughput dropped and many user-facing requests are timing out. Error rate is currently ~18% 5xx/429 over the last 10 minutes. We rolled a small client-side SDK update at 07:40 (v2.1.0) today which increased request volume from a subset of services.

We're attaching a short tail of request ids and traces. Can your team confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something in our rollout? We need an ETA — this is affecting checkout latency and causing customer complaints.

Attaching: request_logs_tail.txt

Thanks,
Jared Park
SRE — Acme Payments

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jared Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood — urgent

Hi Jared — thanks for the alert and the logs. I'm escalating internally now.

Rishi / runtime team — can you take a look at the request ids Jared attached and confirm whether this is a server saturation/fallback or if there's a pattern consistent with client retries? If needed we can temporarily route Acme traffic to a higher-priority pool or enable short-term throttling with Retry-After headers to stop the retry amplification.

Marissa — FYI on the customer impact; they mentioned checkout timeouts. Please hold a line with the account and advise on expected ETA once we have a quick triage.

Jared — we'll update within 30 minutes.

— Soojin
SoojIn Lee
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jared Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood — urgent

Quick summary from initial triage:
- We observe a sharp increase in short-window concurrent requests from a small set of Acme client IPs starting 07:41 PT (right after their SDK rollout).
- Error surface: a mix of 502/503/504 and 429s. 429s correlate with our per-tenant rate limiter tripping under high instantaneous concurrency. 5xx traces show overloaded request queues on a subset of model-serving pods.
- Key signal: client-side retry patterns look identical across many requests (same backoff profile, near-zero initial backoff). This is creating a retry storm where the backend is saturated and responds 5xx/429, which then triggers more immediate retries.

Immediate mitigation we recommend (we can apply within 15 mins):
1) Push a temporary tenant-specific soft-rate limit that returns 429 with Retry-After: 10 for the offending token group (stops immediate retries from flooding the runtime).
2) Enable short-lived routing of Acme to additional capacity pool (burst nodes) for 2 hours.
3) Add a server-side circuit-breaker to return 503 fast for pathological patterns while we coordinate with the client.

I've attached a short slice of request logs and a Grafana sparkline to this note (grafana_dashboard_sparkline.png). We'll also collect a longer trace for postmortem.

— Rishi
Head of Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <infra@acme-payments.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Park <ops@acme-payments.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood — urgent

Thanks for the quick triage. Some extra context from our side: during the SDK v2.1.0 rollout we changed the default retry policy to max_retries=5 and initial_backoff_ms=0 (we did this to improve latency on some transient network errors). It looks like that default had unintended consequences when combined with short client timeouts.

Snippet from SDK config (v2.1.0):
  retries: 5
  initial_backoff_ms: 0
  backoff_multiplier: 1.3

We're happy to rollback the rollout if that will help. We can also ship a targeted config with exponential backoff and jitter within the hour if Redwood needs us to do that. We would appreciate help understanding whether the recommendation is to change client defaults, server-side Retry-After, or both.

Also: given the customer-visible impact, our GTM team is asking for an executive summary and credits for the downtime window. Please confirm next steps.

— Priya
Infrastructure — Acme Payments

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jared Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood — urgent

Looping in leadership and CS execs per Acme's ask for an executive summary and credits.

Questions for leadership:
- Do we accept a short customer credit for the 07:55–09:30 PT window if root cause is confirmed as client retry storm triggered by our SDK defaults not being defensive enough?
- Should we proactively push a server-side opt-in for conservative Retry-After headers to all enterprise customers for the next 72 hours to avoid repeat incidents?

Status update for Acme: Rishi applied a tenant soft-rate limit at 09:12 PT and we routed Acme to burst capacity at 09:20 PT. Error rates returned to baseline around 09:40 PT. Acme will try a rollback of SDK defaults and send an updated build by 13:30 PT.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Jared Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 from Redwood — urgent

Thanks everyone — final notes and immediate actions: 

1) What happened: a combination of a customer-side SDK change (v2.1.0) that set near-zero initial backoff + increased retries, plus a concentrated rollout that hit a subset of our serving fleet. That produced a retry amplification pattern (retry storm) causing both 429s from our per-tenant limiter and 5xx from overloaded queues.

2) Short-term mitigations applied (completed by 09:30 PT):
   • Tenant soft-rate limiting with Retry-After: 10 (applied 09:12 PT).
   • Routed Acme to burst capacity for 2 hours (applied 09:20 PT).
   • Added temporary server-side circuit-breaker for pathological request signatures (09:25 PT).

3) Customer coordination: Acme rolled back to v2.0.3 at 13:18 PT and sent confirmation. They reported reduced error rates and normal latency after rollback; we saw baseline by 09:40 PT post-mitigation.

4) Owner & next steps (action items):
   • Rishi / Runtime: collect full trace set and produce a technical postmortem (draft due 2026-06-17 12:00 PT).
   • Developer UX: propose safer SDK default (initial_backoff_ms >= 50, exponential backoff with jitter) and a warning on rollout docs (owner: connor_obrien, due 2026-06-18).
   • CS / Billing: recommend credit proposal for Acme (Marissa to lead; propose 10% for the impacted window, to be reviewed by finance).
   • Product / Ops: evaluate whether a temporary enterprise-wide conservative Retry-After opt-in option is appropriate (owner: Evelyn Hart; due 2026-06-19).

5) Communications: Draft post-incident note and customer-facing summary attached (postmortem-draft.docx). Marissa, please coordinate the customer-facing message once the postmortem is ready.

I'll escalate to the Exec Ops channel with the above summary. Good work moving fast here.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
